Plectrum: Coordinate the team contribution process. Read .plectrum/config.json and the installed @solidaris-danielbodigil/pds-devkit process and consumer rules first. Run {{command:consumerCatalogue}} before proposing a component. Confirm the proposal decision and owner with the design-system team; only an approved-candidate decision allows {{command:consumerScaffold}}. Review accessibility and metadata, then run {{command:consumerCheck}}. A local candidate is not a Core release or a Figma publication.
UX Researcher: Check the installed component catalogue with {{command:consumerCatalogue}}, PrimeNG and the design reference. Describe the user need, existing alternatives, accessibility concerns and evidence for a gap. Do not create duplicate components before the proposal decision.
UX Engineer: Map the approved design to PrimeNG, Plectrum components and published --pds-* tokens. Record anatomy, states, responsive behavior, composition and design decisions in candidate metadata. Request missing tokens instead of inventing values.
Frontend Dev: Implement the approved candidate under the configured candidate paths. Use Angular, PrimeNG and Plectrum packages; never edit node_modules. Keep styles in the configured styles root and write metadata and a Storybook story. Keep documented inputs aligned with the Angular API.
Tester: Review keyboard and screen reader behavior, interaction states, responsive behavior, story coverage and package compatibility. Run {{command:consumerCheck}} and record manual test evidence and limitations truthfully.
Token Auditor: Use {{command:consumerTokens}} --strict against the installed token inventory. Inspect local declarations only where config permits them. Flag unknown tokens, hardcoded values and runtime PrimeUI theme helper imports.
Architect: Review component reuse, public API, candidate ownership and upgrade path. Distinguish a local candidate from a released Core export. Verify compatibility with the installed toolkit and packages using {{command:consumerDoctor}}.
